question.text: Which of the following accurately describes the permitted fund structures across AIF categories under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: All AIF categories may be open-ended, subject to minimum corpus of INR 20 crore.
Category I AIFs may be open-ended if they invest only in listed equity; Category II and III must be close-ended.
Category III AIFs must be close-ended to qualify for leverage up to 2x NAV; Category I and II may be open-ended.
Category I and Category II AIFs must be close-ended; Category III AIFs may be either open-ended or close-ended at the Manager's discretion at registration.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 13(2) and Regulation 13(3): Cat I and Cat II AIFs must compulsorily be close-ended because their underlying investments (start-ups, PE, private credit, infrastructure) are illiquid. Cat III AIFs can be structured as open-ended or close-ended at registration, depending on strategy. The Trap: Options B and C invert the rule or invent a listed-equity exception. Option D conflates leverage (available to Cat III regardless of open/close) with the fund-type rule. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests Cat I/II close-ended-only as a pitchbook item. XIX-B asks about open-ended Cat III minimum-corpus cures. XIX-C unifies both. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: An open-ended Cat III AIF has a redemption obligation — the Liquidity Management Policy and suspension mechanism under Reg 18A(3) must be drafted carefully. Once corpus dips below INR 20 crore, the fund has 3 months to restore it or compulsorily redeem all investors.
